title: Coordinate formula for the Gaussian Hessian
statement: Let $I$ be finite, $v\ge0$, and $c,z\in\mathbb R^I$. The product Gaussian density Hessian, as a continuous bilinear form, is the sum over $i,j\in I$ of the rank-one forms $(h,k)\mapsto h_jk_i$, each multiplied by $\left((z_i-c_i)(z_j-c_j)/v^2-\delta_{ij}/v\right)\prod_{k\in I}p_v(c_k,z_k)$, where $p_v(a,b)$ denotes the one-dimensional Gaussian density with mean $a$ and variance $v$, and $\delta_{ij}$ is $1$ if $i=j$ and $0$ otherwise.
replaced: Let $I$ be finite and $v\ge0$. Put $G_v(c,z)=\prod_i p_v(c_i,z_i)$, where $p_v$ is the Gaussian density of variance $v$ for $v>0$ and $p_0=0$, and put $S_v(c,z)[h]=\sum_i((z_i-c_i)/v)h_i$, with division by zero equal to zero. Define $A_v(c,z)[h]=G_v(c,z)S_v(c,z)[h]$ and $T_v(c,z)[h,k]=G_v(c,z)(S_v(c,z)[h]S_v(c,z)[k]-\sum_i h_i k_i/v)$. For all $c,z,h,k\in\mathbb R^I$, $T_v(c,z)[h,k]=G_v(c,z)\sum_{i,j}((z_i-c_i)(z_j-c_j)/v^2-\delta_{ij}/v)h_jk_i$, where $\delta_{ij}$ is the Kronecker delta.
